passage: Ten minutes before the annual day dance, Aditi's phone buzzed. Someone had sent her a screenshot: Ishita, her best friend since class six, had told the class group who Aditi liked. Aditi's hands shook. She still had Ishita's old voice note, the one where she cried about her marks, and her thumb hovered over the share button. Then the teacher called the dancers to the wings. Aditi put the phone in her bag, walked out and danced badly. After the show she found Ishita behind the stage and said, "You told my secret. I was so angry I nearly did the same to you, and I didn't. I need time to decide if I can trust you." Ishita went pale and said sorry.

qa.q: What was Aditi's thumb hovering over?
qa.a: It was hovering over the share button of Ishita's old voice note.

qa.q: Why did Aditi want to share the voice note, and what made her change her mind?
qa.a: She wanted to hurt Ishita back for the betrayal, but being called to the wings gave her time to cool down and she chose to speak privately instead.

qa.q: What might Aditi do next about the friendship?
qa.a: She can take the time she asked for, watch whether Ishita's apology is followed by more care with what she shares, and then decide how much to trust.

qa.q: How might Ishita have felt when Aditi said she had nearly done the same?
qa.a: She was probably ashamed and afraid of losing her best friend, seeing how much her telling had hurt.

grounding: A teen feels betrayed and wants to expose her friend back, but cools down, confronts privately and weighs whether trust can be rebuilt.
